definitions.explanation: Physical deformation or distortion of a material caused by stress, pressure, or force. Used in engineering and physics.
Figuratively, the negative effects or imbalances that arise from rapid change, flawed policies, or structural problems in society, relationships, or organizations.

examples.japanese: {金属|きんぞく}に{歪|ひず}みが{生|しょう}じた。
{地震|じしん}で{建物|たてもの}に{歪|ひず}みが{出|で}た。
examples.english: The earthquake caused distortion in the building.

examples.japanese: {温度|おんど}{変化|へんか}による{歪|ひず}みを{最小限|さいしょうげん}に{抑|おさ}える{設計|せっけい}が{求|もと}められる。
examples.english: A design that minimizes distortion from temperature changes is required.

examples.japanese: {社会|しゃかい}の{歪|ひず}みが{問題|もんだい}になっている。
examples.english: The strains in society are becoming a problem.

examples.japanese: {急速|きゅうそく}な{経済成長|けいざいせいちょう}の{歪|ひず}みが{出|で}ている。
examples.english: The negative effects of rapid economic growth are showing.

examples.japanese: {制度|せいど}の{歪|ひず}みを{是正|ぜせい}しないと、{格差|かくさ}はますます{広|ひろ}がるだろう。
examples.english: Unless the distortions in the system are corrected, the gap will continue to widen.

notes:
USAGE:
The same kanji {歪|ゆが}み (read as ゆがみ) exists as a separate entry with overlapping but distinct usage. {歪|ひず}み tends to be preferred in technical and engineering contexts (stress, strain) and in discussions of systemic or structural problems, while {歪|ゆが}み is more common for visible physical warping and subjective distortion.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {歪|ひず}みが{生|しょう}じる (strain develops)
- {歪|ひず}みが{出|で}る (distortion appears)
- {社会|しゃかい}の{歪|ひず}み (strains in society)
- {歪|ひず}みを{是正|ぜせい}する (to correct distortions)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {歪|ゆが}み: distortion, warp — same kanji with a different reading; focuses more on visible deformation
- {偏|かたよ}り: bias, imbalance — emphasizes unevenness rather than deformation
